_: The measured performance bar, read by scripts/gates/perf.py.
The bar itself, the method and the current medians are owned by
docs/architecture/foundation.md section 1 (commitment 2). This file is the
machine-readable copy the gate reads - keep the two in step.
WHY THERE IS A MACHINE CLASS AT ALL:
the budget is wall-clock, and roughly a third of the scan budget is
Tantivy, which uses min(cores, 8) indexing threads. A 2-core CI runner is
plausibly ~3x slower on that phase through no fault of the change under
test. Asserting the 13 s number on such a runner would produce a gate that
fails randomly, and a gate that fails randomly is a gate people learn to
ignore.
So the gate REFUSES TO ASSERT below min_cores rather than scaling the
number by a fudge factor. A skipped measurement is honest; a measurement
adjusted by a guess is not. The refusal applies to every benchmark here,
for the same reason.
THE BENCHMARK SHAPE:
each entry under `benchmarks` names a cargo example and how to drive it.
`args` is a template - {tmpdir} is a scratch directory the gate creates and
removes, {size} the fixture size, {runs} the run count. The example is
expected to run itself `runs` times and print a median line that
`median_pattern` captures, because the example knows what part of its own
work is being measured and the gate does not.
reference_machine: 10-core arm64 darwin (the machine the medians were taken on)
